title: viable/strict/1794563420: [Inductor] optimized FakeTensor metadata refresh (#204337) (#204337)
excerpt: Summary: Human Summary The incremental update that's widely used in the Inductor post-grad passes currently scans all graph nodes with a node-hashing mechanism (based on the args, kwargs) to find changes. Although this is exhaustive and accurate, it is wasteful for compilation time if the caller already knows the root nodes where changes originated. Both updaters stop scheduling users when refreshed output metadata and storage semantics are unchanged; the targeted updater additionally compares aliasing against old and new arguments. The core implementation adds a sibling pass to the incremental_update function, which takes in the extra argument of which root nodes the change started from. It then performs the same propagation mechanisms as the original refresh helper. It also maintains the relevant FakeTensorUpdater states so that calls between this pass and the original are composable. The targeted updater processes a priority worklist in existing FX topological order. Starting from caller-supplied roots avoids the original graph-wide discovery scan, while early stopping bounds downstream propagation once metadata stabilizes. title: trunk/696e48875b7adf797c9b6acfc58212424baf74df: [CPP FakeTensor] Enter and exit the C++ FakeTensorMode (#203093)
excerpt: Implement CppFakeTensorMode context management with one thread-local stack. Each entry saves its mode and restoration state, including reentries of an active or inherited mode. Exit requires the matching top entry on the same thread, then restores the previous mode and lift flag. Reject subclasses before changing state and reject mixing Python and C++ fake modes. Match Python's dispatch-mode detection by saving and setting its existing activity flag when an entry installs a C++ mode, and restoring the flag on exit. Temporary suspension leaves the flag unchanged, while installation without enter does not set it, as for Python FakeTensorMode. Keep balanced, reverse-order context exits. The entry stack records the previous activity flag alongside its other restoration state, without adding another per-mode stack. Detection uses the existing Python flag and Dynamo handling. Cover nesting, reentry, exception restoration, temporary suspension, low-level installation and guarded Dynamo reuse for both fake mode classes. title: trunk/69908d8e41ec875bbbf4729edebbccce2ee7ab37: [dynamo] Raise TypeError for len() of a 0-d tensor (#203515)
excerpt: Linked issue or supporting maintainer Fixes #202895 Supported by @rtimpe BC-breaking? No Summary Calling len() on a 0-dimensional tensor under torch.compile previously leaked an internal IndexError during Dynamo tracing instead of matching PyTorch eager's TypeError . This prevented standard try...except TypeError exception handling in user code and caused compilation to fail. Root Cause TensorVariable.sq_length_impl ( torch/_dynamo/variables/tensor.py ) unconditionally traced size(0) . For 0-d tensors, _method_size_stride indexed an empty size tuple, causing an internal IndexError during tracing. Fix Updated TensorVariable.sq_length_impl to check ndim . When ndim is known to be 0 , Dynamo now explicitly raises TypeError("len() of a 0-d tensor") to match eager Tensor.__len__ . If ndim is unknown, existing behavior is preserved. Test Plan Added unit tests to TestTensorLen in test/dynamo/test_len_protocol.py covering len() , __len__ , and Tensor.__len__ on 0-d tensors, try/except handling with and without fullgraph=True , and uncaught error paths. python test/dynamo/test_len_protocol.py -k TestTensorLen Pull Request resolved: #203515 Approved by: https://github.com/rtimpe

excerpt: Release v5.20.0 New Model additions Muse Spark Open Muse Spark Open is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model from Meta that takes text, images, audio, and video as input and generates text. It has 816B total parameters (42B active per token) and a context window of up to 1,048,576 tokens shared across modalities. It is trained for agentic coding tasks such as multi-file editing, debugging, and tool use. Checkpoints are available in BF16 and NVFP4 formats. Links: Documentation | Blog Post Add Muse Spark Open ( #49644 ) by @guarin in #49644 Ling 3.0 Ling 3.0 Flash is a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts language model from InclusionAI. Its decoder groups five Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) layers with one Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) layer. The MLA blocks use interleaved rotary embeddings and a head-wise output gate, and the feed-forward blocks combine routed and shared experts. It is natively supported in Transformers as BailingHybridForCausalLM , so it loads without trust_remote_code=True . Links: Documentation [Model] Add native Ling 3.0 Flash support ( #49446 ) by @icavan in #49446 Kolibri1 Kolibri 1 is Aleph Alpha's mixture-of-experts reasoning model, focused on German and English. Each of its 50 layers routes every token to 6 of 384 experts using sigmoid routing, and adds one shared expert. Four sliding-window attention layers alternate with one full-attention layer, and RoPE is applied only in the sliding-window layers. Links: Documentation Add Kolibri 1 ( #49463 ) by @lucamotz
